en.html:
Following Muramasa's directions, I was about to run straight through the crossroads—
Then a sight passing across the edge of my vision brought me to a hurried stop.

en.html:
At the far end of the passage.
Two soldiers—and a young man pinning somebody down, astride them.

The captive was a woman.
...Captain Ootori, without question!

My voice must have reached them. The man on top turned one glance my way.

en.html: One short click of the tongue. In that half-instant, the man appeared to settle his assessment.◆—I was a warrior wearing Tsurugi armor. He was lightly equipped; his soldiers, ordinarily equipped.◆—The entire advantage in strength lay on this side. With a locust's movement, he sprang off Lady Kanae. Then he ran down the passage in the opposite direction from me.
en.text:
One short click of the tongue.
In that half-instant, the man appeared to settle his assessment.◆—I was a warrior wearing Tsurugi armor. He was lightly equipped; his soldiers, ordinarily equipped.◆—The entire advantage in strength lay on this side.

With a locust's movement, he sprang off Lady Kanae.
Then he ran down the passage in the opposite direction from me.

ja.html: 短い舌打ち。 　その半瞬に、男は状況を即断した様子だった。◆―― 俺は劒冑を装甲した武者。男は軽武装。彼に従う兵士 も通常装備。◆――戦力優越は完全に当方こちら。 　蝗虫ばったの挙動で男が香奈枝嬢から跳び離れる。 　そのまま俺とは逆方向に、廊下を駆け去っていった。

The man was fast enough. But the Captain's feet were also making very little allowance for the fact that she had been strangled until this very moment.

Shishiku Ootori, the Sasagawa Kubo—his youth exceeded my expectations, and so did the sharp, hard edges of his face.

That was the man Lady Kanae meant to avenge her father upon.

en.html:
Both had already vanished from sight. Even had they remained visible, my decision would have been the same.

I knew why the Captain had not answered my call.
—We had settled this already. Her objective and mine were different. Neither was to assist the other.

Perhaps, in effect, I had just saved her. That was coincidence making its own arrangements, nothing more. Assistance was not what I had undertaken. To pursue them now, however—that would be another matter.

I would be throwing away my own duty,
and obstructing her fight.

ja.html:
両者は既に俺の視野から失せている。
　まだ見えていたとしても、決断は変わらなかった。

　大尉が俺の呼ばわりに反応しなかった、その理由が
わかっている。
　――そう、決めていた事だ。俺と大尉の目的は違う。
互いに助け合いはしない。

　今は結果的に俺が大尉を救ったのかもしれないが、
それは単に偶然の仕様だ。
　協力したわけではない。しかし、更にここから追う
となると、話は変わる。

　俺は自分の責務を投げ捨てて、
　彼女の戦いを妨げる事になる。
